findings.reason: the plan should cite SearchHit and either reuse or extend it (adding arms/parent_documentation) or state why an internal record distinct from the retrieval owner's own hit type is required; as written the two types must be hand-kept in sync and the fork is invisible.
findings.text: §4 (node candidate-retrieval) introduces Candidate with fields path, ids, unit, documentation, node_category, data_type, physics_domain and retrieval_score, all of which SearchHit already carries (SearchHit.path/documentation/units/data_type/ids_name/physics_domain and SearchBase.score at search_strategy.py:86); hybrid_dd_search returns list[SearchHit] (imported at dd_search.py:36), so the candidate record is a second, parallel definition of a hit that the retrieval owner already produces, with only arms and parent_documentation genuinely new

findings.reason: with public_definitions supplied as 0 the section must say in its own text what the field and functions displace (for example §8's free-text mapping_target_path / mapping_target_ids) or why no existing definition can be merged, or the added public surface grows unaccounted.
findings.text: §6 adds one SignalSource field (candidate_route) and two public graph_ops.py functions (write_candidates, clear_candidates) and its "Surface" paragraph accounts only for why the new relationship type cannot merge into MAPS_TO_IMAS, naming nothing the field or the two functions retire or merge and not stating why nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_codex/ids/candidates.py hides the state block, the batched question set, answer parsing, the pair record and the threshold/margin/floor routing behind retrieve_candidates, judge_candidates and route; §7 moves rather than multiplies the seven per-stage claim helpers into three parameterised routines in their existing owner.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the retrieval record is a parallel copy of SearchHit, the type hybrid_dd_search already returns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 this week; §5 and §7 account for their added surface in their own text, but §6 adds a public field and two public graph_ops.py functions while accounting only for the relationship type's non-mergeability.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the maintained owners it would extend and every mechanism it proposes to delete is real: hybrid_dd_search (imas_codex/graph/dd_search.py:97, and its embedding/ids_filter/physics_domain arguments exist), cluster_search (dd_search.py:869, which does path-membership lookup for a slash-containing query, so it genuinely replaces ClusterSearcher.search_by_path at imas_codex/clusters/search.py:200), analyze_units (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:168), the claim owner imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py, the decisions layer call_decisions/acall_decisions (imas_codex/discovery/base/llm.py:3429/3493), run_discovery_engine (imas_codex/discovery/base/engine.py:92) and the three MAPS_TO_IMAS writers (graph_owners.py:357, mapping.py:2085, models.py:580 — a census of exactly three, as §8 claims).
